elements.element: Customer may assign to an affiliate without consent.
elements.evidence: Rendered §XXIV(c): "Licensee may assign this Agreement, without Licensor's consent, to an Affiliate or to a successor..."; "Affiliate" is a defined term at §1.1, so the grant is operative and not dependent on an undefined trigger.

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets without consent.
elements.evidence: Rendered §XXIV(c): "without Licensor's consent, to ... a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all of its assets" — all three transaction types expressly named.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: Rendered §XXIV(c): "Licensor may not assign this Agreement without Licensee's prior written consent"; no retained no-consent exception for Licensor (the affiliate/successor carve-out is expressly Licensee-only), so no new Vendor assignment exception is created.

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor assignment is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: Rendered §XXIV(c): "...without Licensee's prior written consent, which will not be unreasonably withheld..."

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: Rendered §XXIV(c): "and may not assign this Agreement to a competitor of Licensee" — an unconditional bar, not merely a reasonable-consent factor.

elements.element: Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination right.
elements.evidence: Rendered Article XX(a): "A Change of Control (as defined below) shall not give Licensor any right to terminate this Agreement or any of Licensee's rights or licenses hereunder." The automatic-termination-unless-consent mechanic and the deemed-reasonable-refusal (competitive / "adversely effected") language are removed, and the CHANGE OF CONTROL definition ("As used herein...") is retained so the sentence is not dangling.

elements.element: Both parties may assign to a successor.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause gives the successor/affiliate carve-out to Licensee only; Licensor "may not assign this Agreement without Licensee's prior written consent" with no successor exception. To reach the fallback the drafter would have to add an express Licensor successor-assignment right.

elements.element: A successor assignment requires written notice.
elements.evidence: No notice mechanic appears anywhere in the rendered text; Licensee's affiliate/successor assignment is simply "without Licensor's consent" with no obligation to notify.

Although "any other assignment by Licensee requires Licensor's prior written consent," the clause retains a no-consent non-successor exception (assignment to an Affiliate), which under the ASSIGN fallback boundary defeats this element.

elements.element: Consent to other assignments is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: The reasonableness standard is attached only to Licensee's consent to a Licensor assignment; no reasonableness qualifier is attached to Licensor's consent to Licensee's "other" assignments.

reasons: All six preferred elements are met in operative language, so the redline is position-complete at the preferred level; the fallback checklist is deliberately not reached (no mutual successor right, no notice, retained affiliate carve-out, no reasonableness on Licensee's other assignments), which is acceptable because completeness at either level suffices.

Minimality holds: the edit is confined to §XXIV(c) and Article XX(a). Favourable retained language survives (the void-attempt sentence, the successors-and-permitted-assigns sentence, the CHANGE OF CONTROL definition), and no survival tail, expense, notice-procedure or other extra-checklist requirement is bolted on. Deletion of the §XXIV(c) sentence routing Change of Control to "Section 13.4(a)" is within the target scope and necessary to avoid a dangling cross-reference to a non-existent section, so it is not cosmetic surplus.

Intent is preserved: no new Vendor assignment exception is granted (the carve-out runs to Licensee only, satisfying the successor/licence-transfer intent test), the Article XXII right of first refusal and all other commercial mechanics are untouched, and the retained CHANGE OF CONTROL definition keeps the rewritten Article XX(a) self-consistent. The Article XX heading now describes a non-terminating provision, which is cosmetic only and creates no contradiction.

Optional polish (not a defect): if the counterparty pushes back, the fallback offer in the comment would need express operative language for a Licensor successor assignment plus a written-notice trigger and removal of the affiliate carve-out — the comment correctly presents it as a discussion point rather than as drafted text.
